issues.detail: Error handling is thin: the local strategy has no try/catch around async DB calls, the Google callback ignores a missing email, accounts are created without checking for an existing email (risking duplicate or hijacked accounts), and CSRF is only mentioned as a guideline with no implementation.
The examples are prose descriptions of requests and expected responses rather than runnable end-to-end demonstrations, and the password is elided with '...'.

scenarios.name: email-password-login-express
scenarios.rationale: A matches the rubric nearly point for point (express-session with the required options, passport.authenticate('session'), LocalStrategy with usernameField 'email' and bcrypt.compare, serializeUser/deserializeUser, POST logout using req.logout with a callback, and an isAuthenticated middleware that redirects to /login), while B skips Passport and uses manual sessions with session.destroy, so it misses the Passport-specific items even though its session config and bcrypt use are sound.

scenarios.name: google-signin-behind-proxy
scenarios.rationale: Both include the passport-google-oauth20 strategy, env-var credentials, /auth/google and /auth/google/callback routes with profile and email scope, trust proxy 1, and a safe profile.emails access; A sets an absolute callbackURL with proxy:true and a persistent store, which fits the proxy problem better, while B uses a relative callbackURL that may still resolve to http and only suggests an absolute one as a fallback.

scenarios.name: fix-legacy-logout-and-hardening
scenarios.rationale: B covers every rubric item, including bcrypt with cost 12+, env-sourced secrets, CSRF, a persistent store and POST logout with a callback. A omits the bcrypt cost factor (it only says 'argon2 or bcrypt') and gives less explicit emphasis to the Redis store and CSRF, though its code is richer.
